To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
wheat DDGS samples had low AA digestibilities and the SID values were higher than AID values for all AA.
the ileal digestibilities of AA in wheat DDG samples were less than in wheat and the SID values of AA in wheat were greater than those in wheat DDGS.
AID and SID estimates of AA in wheat DDGs samples were significantly lower than those of wheat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the SID of AA in 5 wheat DDGS samples and the wheat sample.
the determination of AID and SID AA values in wheat DDGS fed to broilers and the development of a standardized AA digestibility database.
the first attempt to evaluate the ileal digestible AA values of wheat DDGS for broilers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
wheat DDGS is a low protein feed source with low AA digestibility, and therefore should be considered in diet formulation with caution.
the AID and SID values for AA in wheat DDGs samples were variable and significantly different among samples.
the AA digestibility of wheat is greater than in wheat DDG, and the digestibility of wheat DDG is highly variable among samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SID values of AA in wheat DDG samples are lower than in wheat, but they are higher than in corn DDG samples.
wheat DDGS is a good source of AA for broilers, but it is not as good as wheat.

SID values of indispensable AA in wheat are higher than in wheat distilller's dried grains with solublues (P < 0005) but SID values of indispensable and dispensable AA in wheat distilllers dried grains with soluble are higher than in corn (P < 001).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SID values of indispensable AA in wheat were higher (P < 00001) than in wheat DDG samples.
wheat DDGS is a good source of protein for broilers, and its inclusion rate should be based on the digestibility of the indispensable AA.
the AA digestibility of wheat DDGS varies among samples and is generally lower than wheat.
